chapter_name: Management of Support Services, Institutions and Programmes for Children, Youth and Elderly
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how society cares for its most vulnerable members—children, youth, and the elderly—and the institutions that support them!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Certain groups in society—like orphans, at-risk youth, and the destitute elderly—cannot fulfill their basic needs independently. They require structured support systems to survive and thrive.
Support includes institutions like Observation Homes (for juveniles in conflict with the law), Orphanages, and SOS Children's Villages (which provide a family-like environment for orphans).
Youth need direction and skill development. Programmes like NSS (National Service Scheme), NYKS (Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan), and vocational training centers help channel youth energy positively.
As joint families break down, many elderly face isolation and health issues. Support comes via Old Age Homes, Day Care Centers for senior citizens, and government pension schemes.
Running these support services requires skilled management, empathy, funding, legal knowledge, and a strong focus on the dignity and rehabilitation of the inmates.

fun_activity.title: 🎙️ The Time Traveler Interview
fun_activity.instructions: Interview a grandparent or an elderly neighbor. Ask them what their favorite hobby was when they were your age, and what the biggest change they've seen in society is. This helps build empathy and understanding of gerontology!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the term 'Vulnerable' in a sociological context.
📌 Know the difference between Children in Need of Care and Protection (orphans, abused) and Children in Conflict with the Law (juvenile offenders).
📌 Mention the SOS Children's Villages as a prime example of non-institutional, family-based care.
quick_recap: ⭐ The government, NGOs, and the community must work together to run support services.
⭐ Youth programs aim at character building, citizenship, and skill development.
⭐ Elderly care focuses on financial security, healthcare, and emotional well-being.
